scenarios.name: mild_day_pumps_loafing
scenarios.description: The healthy mild-weather case: 20 degC outdoors and the distribution pumps at 30%. The loop is asking for little and the drives have backed off, which is what a working DP reset looks like.

scenarios.name: cold_day_pumps_working_hard
scenarios.description: NO_EVAL: 0 degC outdoors with the pumps at 80%. The plant is meant to work hard on a design day, so pump speed carries no information about the DP setpoint and yMildWeather = false tells the host not to read yFault as a clean bill of health.

scenarios.name: mild_day_pumps_working_hard
scenarios.description: The fault as PNNL-27338 sec.4.2 writes it: 20 degC outdoors, pumps at 80%. Light load, hard-working pumps, and the alarm lands at exactly alarm_delay because delayOnInit holds the condition from the first tick.

scenarios.name: pump_speed_exactly_at_the_threshold
scenarios.description: Threshold edge from below: the drives sit exactly on high_pump_speed (45%) in mild weather. Reals.GreaterThreshold is strict, so 45.0% is not above 45.0% and nothing is reported.

scenarios.name: pump_speed_just_below_the_threshold
scenarios.description: 44.9% in the same mild weather: still clear, by a tenth of a percent of drive speed.

scenarios.name: pump_speed_just_above_the_threshold
scenarios.description: 45.1% in the same mild weather: the alarm arrives at 3600 s. Both sides of the pump-speed boundary are pinned so the strictness cannot change silently.

scenarios.name: oat_exactly_at_the_mild_weather_floor
scenarios.description: Threshold edge on the evaluability conjunct: outdoor air exactly at mild_weather_oat (15.6 degC) with the pumps at 80%. Strict comparison, so exactly-at-the-floor is NO_EVAL rather than a fault.

scenarios.name: oat_just_below_the_mild_weather_floor
scenarios.description: 15.5 degC with the same hard-working pumps: still NO_EVAL.

scenarios.name: oat_just_above_the_mild_weather_floor
scenarios.description: 15.7 degC with the same hard-working pumps: evaluable, and the alarm lands at exactly alarm_delay. A tenth of a degree of outdoor air is the whole difference between this scenario and the one before last.

scenarios.name: plant_off_in_mild_weather
scenarios.description: The other healthy mild-weather case: the distribution is off and the drive reports 0%. The rule needs no run-status conjunct as long as the speed feedback falls to zero with the pump - a drive that latches its last commanded speed while stopped fabricates this fault, which is why preconditions asks for feedback rather than command.

scenarios.name: morning_warms_through_the_floor
scenarios.description: A spring morning: the pumps run at 80% from midnight and outdoor air crosses 15.6 degC at t = 1800 s. The clock starts at the crossing, not at the start of the run, and the alarm lands at 5400 s.

scenarios.name: pumps_slow_after_alarm
scenarios.description: The repair, seen from the trend: the DP setpoint is reset down at t = 5400 s and the drives fall to 30%. yFault clears on that tick - TrueDelay passes the falling edge with no delay - while yMildWeather stays true, so the host can tell a fix from a weather change.

scenarios.name: evening_cooldown_releases_evaluability
scenarios.description: The weather change, for contrast: an alarming plant sees outdoor air fall to 10 degC at t = 5400 s with the pumps still at 80%. yFault and yMildWeather drop on the same tick and nothing was repaired.

scenarios.name: pump_speed_dips_and_restarts_the_clock
scenarios.description: Persistence is continuous, not accumulated: a 600 s dip to 40% at t = 1800 s discards the elapsed time rather than pausing it, so the alarm lands at 6000 s - one full alarm_delay after the second crossing. PNNL-27338's window average would have carried the dip through instead (see Deviations).

scenarios.name: pumps_slow_on_the_maturity_tick
scenarios.description: Delay edge from below: the condition holds from t = 0 and the drives fall to 30% at exactly 3600 s, the tick the timer matures on. The input is false when the timer comes due, so a full hour of hard pumping in mild weather is never reported.

scenarios.name: pumps_slow_one_tick_later
scenarios.description: Delay edge from above: the same run held 60 s longer asserts at exactly 3600 s and clears at 3660 s. The pair makes the T + delayTime boundary observable rather than assumed.
